text:
elaine: quick question — for routing by customer intent, are we leaning toward propagating an explicit routing header (e.g. `X-Route-Hint`) or deriving hints from a combo of `User-Agent` + auth claims?
vik: short answer: prefer explicit signed hints for critical decisions, but we could still derive for best-effort routing. spoof risk otherwise.
carmen: +1. if we accept unsigned `X-Route-Hint` it can be trivially spoofed by clients and break quotas/tenant isolation. any header we rely on for billing/SLA needs a signature or must come from a trusted edge.
jordan: what about using the auth token (JWT) claims to infer tenant/plan and then use UA as tie-breaker? that avoids extra round-trip to sign but means more parsing on gateway.
elaine: jwt-derive seems ok for tenant->quota mapping, but some partners want explicit opt-in routing (dedicated capacity) per-request. we could support both: signed header for explicit opt-in, jwt-derived fallback.
vik: agree. proposed header contract: `X-Route-Hint: dedicated:pool-alpha` and `X-Route-Signature: <hmac>` where signature = HMAC_SHA256(body|hint, key-id). edge will verify key-id -> public key. unsigned hints are ignored for critical routing.
carmen: important: if signature verification fails, we should emit metric `routing.hint.signature_fail` and fall back to tenant-default routing, not best-effort. Helps detect misconfigured partners.
elaine: console implications: product wants to show per-request "route source" in the request trace (jwt|signed-header|derived-ua). we need a small schema change to traces to include `route_source`.
jordan: also check: UA-derived heuristics will be fuzzy. propose we keep a learning mode where UA-based routing logs decisions but doesn't control production routing until opt-in. Add flag `route.derive.ua = true` for canary customers.
vik: for rollout plan: 1) implement signature verification + metrics 2) add `route_source` field to spans 3) enable signed-header routing for enterprise tenants behind an allowlist 4) run UA-derived in observe-only mode for 2 weeks 5) enable UA-derived as fallback for 5% of traffic -> ramp.
elaine: canary metrics to watch: routing.success_rate, routing.signature_fail_rate, 5xx_by_route, avg_latency_by_route, quota_mismatch_alerts. we should wire these into the console dashboard as a "Routing health" panel.
canary-bot: canary note: enabling UA-derived fallback for tenant `acme-inc` at 2024-06-12T17:00Z per plan.
vik: small implementation notes: keep header parsing at the gateway (very early), but only mutate the request's routing key after verification. avoid doing heavy JWT parsing in the fast path unless we cache parsed claims per connection.
carmen: security: require key rotation policy and have edge reject signatures from unknown key-ids. also limit length/characters of `X-Route-Hint` to a strict regex.
jordan: API for customers: publish a signer library (node/ruby/go) that signs hints and includes `key-id` header. docs + quickstart will be part of the roll out.
elaine: UX question: should product allow users to set per-route fallback priority in console (signed-header > jwt > ua) or keep server-side default?
vik: make it configurable per-tenant but default to safe order (signed > jwt > ua). console can expose it but only editable by admins.
carmen: follow-ups: I'll draft the header spec + signature format and a short security checklist. can someone own the dashboard widgets?
jordan: I can do the dashboard. will need the metric names and sample spans.
elaine: thanks — can we reconvene in #eng-platform tomorrow after the spec draft?
ops-bot: deploybot: created ticket INF-1834 for "Signed routing hints: spec + gateway verification" assigned to carmen.
elaine: perfect, tagging @vik @jordan for visibility. :thumbsup:
